A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same feature-resonance/RSL work despite changed titles and formatting. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison and matching of relocated content.

before.justification: v1 reports original toy experiments, five-dataset node-detection results, ablations, timing measurements and representation analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical results and adds node-level, graph-level and image evaluations, together with new controlled analyses.

M1.justification: The core node-level RSL algorithm, losses, resonance scoring and synthetic-node procedure remain unchanged. The new image application in Appendix F.7 introduces a limited adaptation: it aligns pretrained image features to their known-ID mean, whereas v1 specifies randomly generated alignment targets.

E1.justification: v2 adds Cora, Citeseer, Pubmed and Chameleon to the original five node datasets. It also introduces graph-level detection using ENZYMES/PROTEINS and ClinTox/LIPO, plus CIFAR-10-based image detection against standard and harder OOD datasets, substantially expanding domains and task granularity.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds NodeSafe and GRASP under both true-label and pseudo-label settings while retaining the earlier comparators. New comparisons also evaluate methods absent from v1's benchmark tables, including GPN, graph-kernel and contrastive-learning detectors, GOOD-D variants, and image methods such as CSI, SSD+ and KNN+.

E3.justification: New protocols vary supervised-pretraining label proportions, rewire Citeseer edges to alter homophily, and compare GCN/GAT/GIN encoders. Graph-level evaluation introduces 90% ID training with balanced ID/OOD testing; image evaluation uses ResNet-18 features trained with cross-entropy or supervised contrastive loss. The original five-dataset splits and metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Tables 4, 5 and 12 newly test sensitivity to available labels, graph homophily and encoder choice. These directly investigate representation initialization and structural dependence. The earlier classifier/synthesis ablations, target-vector comparisons, sliding-window analyses and visualizations are retained, sometimes relocated.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages over five runs; no increase in runs is established. v2 newly reports ± quantities for graph-level results in Table 13, but does not define their statistical meaning. Its checklist's affirmative statistical-significance answer supplies no additional test or uncertainty procedure.

E6.justification: Matched original scores and plot contents remain unchanged, but v2 adds substantial results in Tables 3–5 and 12–15, including RSL's 94.14 AUROC on Cora and 72.03±2.87 on ClinTox/LIPO. The reported headline FPR95 reduction changes from 18.51% to 15.20% alongside expanded comparisons; this is not a same-setting improvement.

T1.justification: v2 removes v1's explicit task and wild-data definitions, including the Huber-mixture equation in Section 2. The resonance definitions, error bounds, assumptions, proofs, ETF mathematics and feature-change derivation are retained after relocation or renumbering. The added information-bottleneck discussion provides explanatory motivation rather than a new proven guarantee.

C1.justification: The central claims about feature resonance, RSL and OOD separability remain. v2 explicitly broadens the applicability claim to settings without a defined classification pretext task, whereas v1 primarily motivates the work through unavailable multi-category node labels.

C2.justification: v2 adds an information-bottleneck interpretation of mid-training resonance and explains supervision and homophily effects through representation quality. Appendix G.4 newly discusses dependence on validation data, uncertain cross-domain applicability and limited direct use of available labels. These substantially extend v1's discussion, which focused mainly on distinctions from gradient-based methods.

D1.justification: v2 adds a repository link, explicitly identifies the GCN backbone, and documents hyperparameters and processing details for additional evaluations. The original hardware, software, hyperparameters and timing results are retained. Code-access statements are inconsistent: the abstract and checklist promise code, while checklist item 13 says no new code is released.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning around independence from classification pretext tasks. It discusses newer node detectors including NodeSafe, GRASP, GOLD, EDBD and DeGEM, adds graph-level comparator families, and connects resonance to information-bottleneck and feature-learning literature. This exceeds bibliographic updating or isolated citation additions.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introductory motivation and related-work narrative are revised. v2 removes the standalone preliminaries, consolidates the main experimental discussion, moves several analyses into the appendix, and reorganizes discussion material into expanded subsections. It also adds acknowledgements and a conference checklist.

P2.justification: The document switches from a two-column ICML layout to a predominantly single-column NeurIPS layout. v1 Figures 1–2 are combined into v2 Figure 1; several plots and the timing table move to the appendix. Existing plot images are retained, while multiple new result tables and expanded dataset/comparator tables substantially change presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation by adding newer competitors, controlled tests of supervision, homophily and encoder dependence, and evaluations beyond node detection. These address important uncertainties about the method's comparative strength and applicability; explicit validation-set limitations also improve transparency. Undefined uncertainty quantities, removal of formal preliminaries and inaccurate checklist statements weaken reporting, but do not outweigh the substantial gains in empirical scrutiny.
